Agreement No. CE 33/2021 (CE)
Development at Ngau Tam Mei Area
Environmental Impact Assessment Report
13 HAZARD TO LIFE
13.1 Introduction
13.1.1 This section evaluates the hazard to life impacts arising from any existing hazardous
facilities with their consultation zones encroaching upon the Project Site, and any
planned hazardous facilities proposed by the Project. The requirements for assessing
hazard to life are outlined in Annex 4 of the Technical Memorandum on Environmental
Impact Assessment Process (EIAO-TM) and Section 3.4.13 and Appendix L of the
EIA Study Brief (ESB-363/2023).
13.2 Environmental Legislation, Standards and Guidelines
13.2.1 The estimated risk levels shall be compared with the individual and societal risk
criteria set out in the Hong Kong Risk Guidelines (HKRG) to determine the
acceptability of the risk levels.
Hong Kong Risk Guidelines
13.2.2 Individual risk is the predicted increase in the chance of fatality per year to an
individual due to a potential hazard. The individual risk guidelines require that the
maximum level of off-site individual risk should not exceed 1 in 100,000 per year i.e.
1×10-5 per year.
13.2.3 Societal risk refers to the risks to the whole population. It is expressed in terms of
lines plotting the cumulative frequency (F) of number of fatalities (N) or more deaths
in the off-site population from incidents at the installation against N. Two F-N risk lines
are used in the HKRG that demark “Acceptable” or “Unacceptable” societal risks. To
avoid major disasters, there is a vertical cut-off line at the 1,000 fatality level extending
down to a frequency of 1 in a billion years (i.e. 1×10-9 per year). The intermediate
region indicates that the acceptability of societal risk is borderline and should be
reduced to a level which is “as low as reasonably practicable” (ALARP). It seeks to
ensure that all practicable and cost-effective measures that can reduce risk are
considered. The HKRG is presented graphically in Exhibit 13.1.
13-1 August 2025

Development at Ngau Tam Mei Area
Environmental Impact Assessment Report
Exhibit 13-1 Societal Risk Guidelines
13.3 Evaluation of Potential Hazard to Life Impacts
13.3.1 According to the EIA Study Brief, hazard to life assessment would be required to
evaluate the potential impacts due to the existing and/or planned hazardous facilities
(if any) during construction and operational stages of the Project.
13.3.2 Ngau Tam Mei Water Treatment Works (NTMWTW) is situated at approximately 170
m east from the Development Area. As advised by Water Supplies Department, there
is no liquid chlorine storage in NTMWTW. Therefore, NTMWTW is not considered as
hazardous facility, and there would not be any hazards related to storage of liquid
chlorine.
13.3.3 According to the Recommended Outline Development Plan of the Project, there are
no planned hazardous facilities within the Development Area. Therefore, no hazard
to life impact would be arisen from the operation of the Project.
13.4 Mitigation Measures
13.4.1 Mitigation measures are deemed not necessary as no hazard to life impact is
anticipated.
13.5 Conclusion
13.5.1 No hazard to life impact is anticipated as there are no existing hazardous facilities
with their consultation zones encroaching upon the Project Site and no planned
hazardous facilities proposed under the Project.
13-2 August 2025
